mappings.tier3_evidence_ref: concept_note.md — 'MSCA-PF mandatory transferable dimensions: digital and AI skills — including the responsible use of generative AI in environmental modelling and scientific coding — together with knowledge valorisation and innovation/entrepreneurship and research integrity and open-science ethics (FAIR data management, open research software, reproducible validation)'; strategic_positioning.md Section 2.1 — '≥120 hours of transferable-skills training; co-supervision of ≥1 MSc thesis at the host; follow-on national or ERC-track proposal submitted within six months of the fellowship's end'
mappings.mapping_description: The concept explicitly describes comprehensive development of research and transferable skills through a structured programme: ≥120 hours of transferable-skills training, digital and AI skills (including responsible use of generative AI in environmental modelling and scientific coding), knowledge valorisation, innovation/entrepreneurship, and research integrity/open-science ethics (FAIR data management, open research software, reproducible validation). A Career Development Plan (CDP) is prepared jointly by supervisor and fellow and submitted as a project deliverable at months 2–3, then reviewed and updated at M12 and M24. Career development milestones are explicit: ≥3 peer-reviewed publications (≥2 first-author), co-supervision of ≥1 MSc thesis at the host, and a follow-on national or ERC-track proposal submitted within six months of the fellowship's end. The concept advances the fellow from postdoctoral researcher toward independent research leadership. The term 'transferable skills' appears verbatim.

mappings.tier3_evidence_ref: concept_note.md — 'Fellowship type — European Fellowship (EF), 24 months (Plovdiv, Bulgaria → ELTE, Hungary; intra-EU)'; concept_note.md — 'Two-way transfer of knowledge. The fellow brings plant-physiology and non-destructive stress-phenotyping expertise...into the host's geoinformatics group'; concept_note.md — 'Associated partner — AgroVIR (Hungary): farmer access, field validation and feedback at Hungarian tomato sites'
mappings.mapping_description: The concept describes an international move (Dr. Rositsa Cholakova, Plovdiv, Bulgaria → ELTE, Budapest, Hungary; intra-EU European Fellowship) constituting the international dimension; a clear interdisciplinary pairing of a plant-physiology fellow in a geoinformatics/remote-sensing host group constituting the interdisciplinary dimension; and inter-sectoral engagement through associated partner AgroVIR (Hungarian tomato growers, non-academic sector providing farmer access and field feedback) constituting the inter-sectoral dimension. Inference chain: The concept describes [an international mobility move from Bulgaria to Hungary as a European Fellowship] and [an interdisciplinary combination of plant physiology with remote sensing/geoinformatics] and [inter-sectoral engagement with non-academic partner AgroVIR], which together constitute the international, inter-sectoral and interdisciplinary experience through which new mind-sets and approaches to R&I work are forged (EO-02).

mappings.tier3_evidence_ref: strategic_positioning.md Section 2.2 — 'Dissemination, exploitation and communication'; 'Target groups are the host's geoinformatics/remote-sensing community and Hungarian tomato growers reached through the associated partner AgroVIR'; 'open research software, open validation data and protocol, peer-reviewed publication'; strategic_positioning.md Section 1.3 — '≥2 methods seminars delivered at the host'; strategic_positioning.md Section 2.1 — '≥3 peer-reviewed publications (≥2 first-author)'
mappings.mapping_description: The concept describes dissemination and communication activities including ≥3 peer-reviewed publications (≥2 first-author), open research software and open validation data and protocol, and ≥2 methods seminars delivered at the host. Outreach extends to Hungarian tomato growers through associated partner AgroVIR and to the host's geoinformatics/remote-sensing community. A 'Dissemination, exploitation and communication' section is explicitly defined in the strategic positioning. Inference chain: The concept describes [≥3 peer-reviewed publications and ≥2 methods seminars at the host institution] which are the mechanisms for enhanced communication with scientific peers, and [outreach to Hungarian tomato growers via AgroVIR and open software/data releases] which constitute communication with a broader stakeholder audience, together addressing EO-03 enhanced networking and communication capacities.

No direct coverage found in the concept corpus. The concept does not reference the European Charter for Researchers or describe specific measures to align working conditions for researchers. The project participates in the MSCA-PF instrument, which requires participating organisations to align working conditions with the Charter as an instrument-level obligation, but the concept does not explicitly describe any mechanism, commitment, or activity relating to working condition alignment. Assumption: assumed to be covered by ELTE's institutional obligations as an MSCA-PF host organisation, which is an implicit instrument-level requirement not requiring explicit treatment in the concept note.

mappings.tier3_evidence_ref: concept_note.md — 'A Career Development Plan is prepared jointly by supervisor and fellow and submitted as a project deliverable at the start of the action (by months 2–3), then reviewed and updated at M12 and M24. Training integrates digital and AI skills...knowledge valorisation and innovation/entrepreneurship...research integrity and open-science ethics'; strategic_positioning.md Section 1.3 — 'Supervision is structured around a Career Development Plan prepared jointly by supervisor and fellow...regular research reviews, and a genuine two-way transfer'
mappings.mapping_description: The concept explicitly describes structured supervision arrangements and a comprehensive training programme. The Career Development Plan is 'prepared jointly by supervisor and fellow and submitted as a project deliverable at the start of the action (by months 2–3), then reviewed and updated at M12 and M24' — this is verbatim from concept_note.md. Supervision is structured around the CDP and 'regular research reviews' (strategic_positioning.md Section 1.3). Training activities address: digital and AI skills, knowledge valorisation, research integrity, and FAIR data practices. The training programme is formalised with ≥120 hours of transferable-skills training. The M12 and M24 review cadence demonstrates sustainability of the training and supervision structure over the fellowship duration.

mappings.tier3_evidence_ref: strategic_positioning.md Section 3.2 — 'ELTE (Budapest, Hungary) — Faculty of Informatics, Institute of Cartography and Geoinformatics — hosts the fellowship'; strategic_positioning.md Section 2.2 — 'Dissemination, exploitation and communication'; strategic_positioning.md Section 2.1 — '≥3 peer-reviewed publications (≥2 first-author)'; project_summary.json — supervisor 'Dr. András Jung...co-founder of Cubert GmbH (hyperspectral cameras) and Brightic Research'
mappings.mapping_description: The concept describes hosting an internationally mobile researcher (European Fellowship, Bulgaria → Hungary) and producing ≥3 peer-reviewed publications, open research software, and open validation data at ELTE — activities through which the participating organisation gains increased global visibility. Inference chain: The concept describes [ELTE hosting an internationally mobile MSCA-PF fellow from Bulgaria, placing ELTE in an international fellowship network] and [producing ≥3 peer-reviewed publications and open research software/data attributed to the ELTE host group] which are the activities through which ELTE's global attractiveness, visibility and reputation in the geoinformatics/remote-sensing domain are increased (EO-06). The supervisor Dr. András Jung's profile (co-founder of Cubert GmbH, multisensor-drone fusion working group) and ELTE's hosting of an internationally mobile fellow are the concrete mechanisms.

mappings.tier3_evidence_ref: concept_note.md — 'Two-way transfer of knowledge. The fellow brings plant-physiology and non-destructive stress-phenotyping expertise (the biological ground truth) into the host's geoinformatics group; the host provides geoinformatics, remote-sensing and hyperspectral/multisensor-fusion methods and infrastructure in return'; strategic_positioning.md Section 1.3 — 'genuine two-way transfer: the fellow brings plant-physiology and non-destructive stress-phenotyping expertise...takes up the host's remote-sensing, hyperspectral and multisensor-fusion competences'; strategic_positioning.md Section 2.1 — '≥3 peer-reviewed publications'
mappings.mapping_description: The concept explicitly describes a 'Two-way transfer of knowledge' as a core structural element: the fellow brings plant-physiology and non-destructive stress-phenotyping expertise into the host's geoinformatics group, and the host provides remote-sensing, hyperspectral and multisensor-fusion methods and infrastructure in return. 'Transfer of knowledge' appears verbatim. R&I capacity at ELTE is strengthened through a new probabilistic-fusion methodology, new peer-reviewed publications (≥3), a TRL 3–4 research prototype, and open research software. The R&I output is concretely specified: ≥3 peer-reviewed publications (≥2 first-author), a research prototype, open research software, and open validation data.

mappings.tier3_evidence_ref: strategic_positioning.md Section 2.1 — 'co-supervision of ≥1 MSc thesis at the host'; strategic_positioning.md Section 1.3 — '≥2 methods seminars delivered at the host, evidenced by ≥2 methods seminars delivered at the host'
mappings.mapping_description: The concept describes co-supervision of ≥1 MSc thesis at the host institution (ELTE) and ≥2 methods seminars delivered at the host, which are the mechanisms through which research results are fed back into teaching and education at the participating organisation. Inference chain: The concept describes [co-supervision of ≥1 MSc thesis at ELTE] and [≥2 methods seminars delivered at the host institution] which constitute the activities through which the research results of the uncertainty-aware irrigation decision framework are fed back into teaching and educational activities at the participating organisation, satisfying EO-08. 'Teaching' is mentioned in the CDP scope ('teaching' appears in strategic_positioning.md Section 1.3 in the context of the training plan).
